questionText:
The statement $( eg p) \Rightarrow ( eg q)$ is logically equivalent to which of the statements below?

I. $p \Rightarrow q$
II. $q \Rightarrow p$
III. $( eg q) \lor p$
IV. $( eg p) \lor q$
explanation:
Given Statement:
$( eg p) \Rightarrow ( eg q)$

Step 1: Using the Implication Equivalence ($A \Rightarrow B \equiv eg A \lor B$)
$( eg p) \Rightarrow ( eg q) \equiv eg( eg p) \lor ( eg q) \equiv p \lor ( eg q) \equiv ( eg q) \lor p$
This matches Statement III.

Step 2: Using the Contrapositive Law ($A \Rightarrow B \equiv eg B \Rightarrow eg A$)
$( eg p) \Rightarrow ( eg q) \equiv eg( eg q) \Rightarrow eg( eg p) \equiv q \Rightarrow p$
This matches Statement II.

Therefore, the given statement is logically equivalent to II and III.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
